name: What should be included in a whole-house remodeling contract?

mainEntity.name: What contract details protect me from disputes on a large remodel?
mainEntity.text: What contract details protect me from disputes on a large remodel?

acceptedAnswer.text: A strong whole-house remodeling contract should be detailed enough that both sides understand exactly what is included. The scope should list rooms, materials, finishes, fixture allowances, labor, permits, cleanup, and any design or engineering services. It should also define the payment schedule, expected timeline, inspection milestones, and how delays are handled. Change orders deserve special attention because whole-house remodels often evolve once work begins. The contract should explain how extra work is approved, priced, and documented. Exclusions should also be written clearly so there is no confusion about what is not included in the price. Homeowners should also look for warranty terms, site protection requirements, and who is responsible for purchasing long-lead materials. The more precise the contract, the easier it is to avoid arguments and keep the project moving.
acceptedAnswer.description: The contract should clearly define scope, allowances, timeline, payment schedule, change order process, exclusions, warranty, cleanup, permits, and who is responsible for design or engineering. Vague contracts are the biggest source of remodel disputes.
